newsitem.title: UK: Brown asks NAO to probe UK financial forecasts.
newsitem.headline: Brown asks NAO to probe UK financial forecasts.

text.p: Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said on Tuesday he had asked the National Audit Office to report within two weeks on the key assumptions and conventions that lie behind forecasts of the public finances.

The Treasury said the NAO, a government auditing watchdog, would review the assumptions adopted for economic growth, unemployment, and interest rates and the conventions used for projecting privatisation proceeds and "spend to save" measures.
Brown told Parliament his move was needed to enhance the credibility of the public finances.
"I believe not only in sound public finance, but in honesty and openness in public finance," Brown said.
"There is no place for hiding behind obscure forecasting assumptions. It is time to rebuild public trust about the management and use of public money."
